190 UK light traps, 2,326 trap-years. Trends are within sites and allow for temperature and rainfall. The steeper urban drop could partly be chance (p = 0.19); fewer moths in cities is robust (p = 0.01).

01Causes

Four city habits, one moth

Set how built-up the area is, how bright the nights are, how gardens are kept and whether pesticides are used. Each wing stands for one habit and sheds its dust by as much as the data says that habit cuts moths.

02Consequences

When moths go, others follow

Moths feed the birds that sing at dawn and the bats that patrol at night, and they pollinate in the dark while bees sleep. Pick a story to explore what happens as moths disappear.

Each story has two more to follow inside it.

03How to help

How to Help

Unlike the climate or the ocean, moths live on our street. Most of what they need is decided garden by garden, so small changes add up fast. Pick an idea to see why it works and how to start.
